intro:
Task 3 implementation is ready for independent review. Three of four CEv1
criteria have valid technical evidence; update-latency remains NOT_VERIFIED. Independent review has not been performed. No delivery action is authorized.

The user authorized a fresh read-only capture of the three JSONL roots and two
SQLite databases, then explicitly selected that frozen copy as the new E2
baseline. The older 12.045s in-place observation remains historical; its exact
input and database starting state are unavailable and it is not relabelled.

The new capture contains 4,630 JSONL files, 826,827,617 bytes; corpus manifest
SHA-256 is `bc4d96dcf8d317b9ca1aff61cd983b2b37bf2d67a5dad484b19873227212456e`.
Database backup SHA-256 values are
`21e35ffea607b6f51faadc28ee9e506586dbfe00a693788f26a016396a895508`
(core) and `3c023609c0310d3a5d846c40494f73cf1b3623310fc569f04041d46d044c148e`
(sessions). No authentication files were captured. Private paths and source
content are excluded from durable records.

sections.title: Source impact and migration boundary
sections.facts:
The partition cache is derived data, not a replacement fact store. Its key is
UTC event day, client and model; the algorithm/parser, core epoch and current-price fallback identify the cached
payload version. Local calendar filters are applied after partition selection. Event insert/delete/update invalidates both old
and new contributions transactionally. Session spans, run bindings and routes
commit coalesced scoped dirty markers with the facts. The projector flushes
those markers atomically before reuse; pending markers and metadata revision
changes reject publication. Pricing and provider timeline operations invalidate
all pricing-dependent partitions. Provider-operation changes also advance the
serving revision. Explicit UPSERT conflict clauses keep marker coalescing safe
inside outer provider UPSERTs.

Existing readers in usage summaries, statistics, presentation, session usage,
signals and desktop keep their canonical `usage_events` joins. Source writers,
orphan cleanup, rewrite and parser rebuild keep their existing logical IDs and
transaction boundaries. The full presentation path remains the oracle. The
incremental reader is selected only by the background desktop projector. Existing
reducers retain their independent distinct sets, median, peak and top semantics;
no daily averages or medians are summed. Deterministic per-event pricing errors
are exposed only when the event enters the selected local window, including
UTC partition tails that fall outside a local calendar boundary.

Migration adds only derived tables/triggers, without replacing facts, session
FTS or external IDs. SQLite backup includes the cache naturally; restore mints
a different core epoch, which is part of the cache version. Older clients keep
the existing schema-ahead failure policy. Read-only clients continue using the
full oracle without creating or migrating state. No live database migration is
part of the experiment; migration and concurrency checks use private fixtures.

Shadow cache publication retains the active payload while a replacement is
built. Publication compares the input revision in a short transaction; a fact
write during derivation rejects the replacement. Existing serving publications
remain independent and readable throughout.

sections.title: Affected session views
sections.facts:
Small updates materialize visible FTS documents only for logical sessions in
changed or removed source paths. Ownership is still ranked across every source
for each selected session. A rewrite that introduces an existing session ID
reconstructs its pre-write winner from unchanged sources. More than 128 changed
paths or old session keys retain the full-view oracle path. The transaction
rebuild path remains an independent full-view oracle.

Source, event and external IDs remain unchanged. Regression coverage compares
scoped counts against complete before/after views for append, duplicate owners,
rewrites introducing another existing ID, deletion, multiple IDs and moves.

sections.title: Serving and native compatibility
sections.facts:
Schema 32 changes only derived storage. Go and Swift accept a schema-31 saved
publication against schema 32 with the same epochs and state identity, mark it
stale, and retain its date. The exception is directional: 32 to 31, 30 to 32,
and 31 to an unknown future schema remain invalid. Swift accepts current schema
32 and retains a full schema-31 view during a narrower schema-32 publication.

The new dependency triggers initially increased cold read-only schema parsing
under race instrumentation and exposed the existing 200ms identity deadline.
A counterfactual schema-31 control passed five runs; the final compact marker
journal and reused generation triggers passed the same serving preservation test
five times without changing its deadline. The broad related race suite also
passed with package concurrency restricted to one. These are correctness checks,
not native latency observations.

The native XCTest run passed 302 tests, one explicitly skipped acceptance test,
zero failures. It includes the new coordinator schema transition test. Wire v1
fixtures were regenerated through their producers; only schema health values
changed to 32. Earlier stale fixture expectations and the marker UPSERT conflict
were corrected rather than waived.

sections.title: E2 evidence boundary
sections.facts:
`scripts/scan-performance-incremental.py` compares the full-fact/full-view oracle
with partition reuse and affected-session views in private source exports. Both
arms use identical schema-32 database seeds and the same fsynced synthetic delta.
It validates presentation/summary, work signals, session periods, full visible
FTS digests and published today totals. Timing ends at the shared engine's
committed serving JSON; it does not measure a native popover frame or watcher
latency. Page cache is not purged. All attempts and limitations remain explicit.

Two early oracle arms failed before a valid pair was obtained (108.11s and
126.51s). Investigation found a harness admission defect: resolving the root
changed `/var/folders` to `/private/var/folders`, while seed source paths used the
former namespace. The failed arm replayed all 4,631 sources and read 826,828,300
bytes; preserving the namespace read only the 352-byte synthetic delta. Four
instrumented same-namespace replays completed. The corrected harness preserves
the stored namespace and rejects any cohort other than exactly one append before
timing. Those two wrong-starting-state executions remain admission failures,
not valid update-latency samples.

engine_comparison.oracle_equivalence: 40/40 full presentation/summary, work signals, session periods, visible FTS digests and published today totals; source mutation exactly one append in every arm
engine_comparison.scope: Full local shared-engine round through committed serving JSON; no native frame/watcher latency or aggregate App/collector resource claim
